title: Nazim Hussain v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Sadhna Rani (Thakur), J.
disposition: Writ disposed without merits; petitioner to file Clause 8.1 objection; assessing officer to decide by speaking order.
headnote: On a challenge to a provisional assessment, the consumer claimed an undecided objection and the licensee denied that any objection had been filed; neither a final assessment nor a demand was produced. Without entering the merits, the Division Bench disposed of the writ by giving the petitioner three weeks to file an objection under Clause 8.1(a)(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If filed, the assessing officer must pass a reasoned speaking order on all points of objection, and any existing final assessment or demand would remain subject to that decision.
facts: Nazim Hussain challenged Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited's provisional assessment dated 2 September 2020, claiming he had filed an objection on 19 February 2020 which was never decided. The licensee's written instructions denied that any objection had been filed. Neither a final assessment nor a demand notice was produced. The petitioner then sought one opportunity to object and to be heard under Clause 8.1(a)(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.topic: provisional assessment — time-bound objection and speaking order
holding_units.holding: Without entering the merits of a challenge to a provisional assessment, the Court directed the petitioner to file an objection within three weeks; if filed, respondent no. 2 must decide it by a reasoned speaking order dealing with all points of objection; any final assessment or demand already issued would be subject to that fresh decision; failing timely filing, the licensee could proceed in accordance with law.

principle_tags.application: Where a consumer challenges a provisional assessment and seeks a Clause 8.1 hearing, the Court may, without deciding merits, permit a time-bound objection and require the assessing officer to pass a reasoned speaking order, with any existing final assessment or demand remaining subject to that decision.

not_decided.point: whether the petitioner had already filed an objection on 19.2.2020
not_decided.note: licensee denied any objection; Court did not resolve the conflict

not_decided.point: merits of the provisional assessment dated 2.9.2020
not_decided.note: Court expressly declined to enter the merits
